clusters.headline_hint: US rejects Iranian peace proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz as tensions flare

claims.text: US President Donald Trump stated on September 27, 2026, that he expects talks with Iran to resume in the coming week despite rejecting Tehran's truce proposal.
Iranian officials brought a plan to the UN General Assembly in New York for a seven-day truce followed by the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
Donald Trump told Axios that Iran wants to make a deal, but 'it is not the deal that I want to make.'
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that any move toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent upon Iran's conditions being met.
US UN Ambassador Mike Waltz accused Iran of making a cynical attempt by demanding the release of the blockade, sanctions, and access to billions in assets just to talk.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards stated that they seized an American submersible drone in the Strait of Hormuz on September 27, 2026.
Tehran stated that it is awaiting a definitive response from Washington through mediators regarding its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Hossein Mohebi, a spokesman for Iran's Revolutionary Guards, was quoted by Tasnim news agency as saying Iran will not cease punishing the US until its seven conditions are met.
Hossein Mohebi stated in an interview that ending hostilities in Yemen was among Tehran's demands.
US Centcom spokesman Captain Tim Hawkins rejected claims that Iran seized an American underwater drone, stating the US retains positive control of all operational drone assets.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it captured an advanced US unmanned underwater vehicle, identified as the Remus 600, in the Strait of Hormuz.
Earlier in September 2026, the IRGC captured a US uncrewed submarine identified as a Dive-LD near the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz.
US UN Ambassador Mike Waltz stated that Donald Trump raised concerns with Chinese Premier Xi Jinping regarding Chinese assistance to Iran in missile targeting.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated on CBS's Face the Nation that Iran is ready for talks on its nuclear program but will not accept bullying or coercion.

clusters.headline_hint: Mass shootings near Johannesburg and Cape Town leave 27 dead in South Africa

claims.text: At least 27 people were killed in two mass shootings across South Africa involving attacks at a tavern near Johannesburg and a shop outside Cape Town.
Seventeen people were killed and 15 injured when eight gunmen stormed a bar near Johannesburg on Saturday evening.
Ten people were killed and 11 injured outside an entertainment venue in a township near Cape Town early Sunday morning.
Gauteng Police Commissioner Lt Gen Tommy Mthombeni stated that citizens from Ethiopia and Lesotho were among those caught up in the Johannesburg shooting.
Days before the weekend shootings, 11 people were killed when gunmen stormed a house in KwaMakhutha township near Durban.
South Africa records about 60 murders every day in a population of 62 million people.
Police reported that 17 people were shot dead at a tavern outside Johannesburg by suspects armed with assault rifles.
Eight suspects armed with AK-47 assault rifles and pistols opened fire at a bar in Wedela township, about 50 miles southwest of central Johannesburg.
Gunmen entered a shisanyama venue in Lwandle near Cape Town at about 1:46 am on Sunday and opened fire on customers.
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa stated on local TV news that the level of criminality must be brought down by security forces.
More than 22,700 people were murdered in South Africa in the 12 months leading up to June 30.
A mass shooting on Tuesday in KwaMakhutha township south of Durban killed 11 people, including a pregnant woman, at a house party.
A tenth woman's body was discovered in Ekurhuleni east of Johannesburg on Saturday amid a spate of brutal femicides.

clusters.headline_hint: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic resigns amid prolonged protests to run for prime minister

claims.text: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic resigned on September 27, 2026, to run for prime minister in a snap parliamentary election scheduled for October 25.
Parliament Speaker Ana Brnabic will serve as acting president of Serbia pending a presidential election.
Aleksandar Vucic pardoned 49 people, including 23 convicted in connection with anti-government protests, as one of his final acts in office.
The political crisis in Serbia followed demonstrations triggered by the collapse of a concrete railway station canopy in Novi Sad on November 1, 2024, which killed 16 people.
A student-led movement called 'Students Win' is contesting the parliamentary election against Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party.
The average net monthly salary in Serbia was 1,032 euros ($1,174) in April, compared with 1,555 euros ($1,770) in neighbouring Croatia.
Aleksandar Vucic stated outside the presidential building in Belgrade that his administration had preserved peace and stability during his nine-year tenure.
Under Serbia's constitution, presidential elections must be held no more than three months after a president's resignation.
Aleksandar Vucic is constitutionally barred from seeking a third term as president of Serbia.
The independent Bureau for Social Research in Serbia filed a complaint alleging Vucic abused a public institution as president to promote his party.
Aleksandar Vucic told state television RTS that foreign powers and unidentified people inside Serbia planned to stir unrest on election night.
Aleksandar Vucic stepped down on Sunday, paving the way for him to run as the Serbian Progressive Party's candidate for prime minister.

clusters.headline_hint: Five arrested near UK RAF air base used by US forces on suspicion of terror and explosives plot

claims.text: A local resident called 999 at around 1:00 am Sunday after spotting three white vans and a large group of hooded and balaclavaed men in Whelford near RAF Fairford.
Police evacuated residents from about 85 households in Whelford to a nearby leisure centre in Cirencester at 6:00 am on Sunday.
Counter-terrorism police, army bomb disposal units, and explosives experts investigated three vans near RAF Fairford.
Five men were arrested near RAF Fairford on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences.
US and UK leaders stated that the arrested men were under investigation and planning to cause 'big damage.'
Police received a call at 12:45 am local time regarding three suspicious white vans travelling towards RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire.
Armed officers arrested five men under the Explosives Act and further arrested them on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act.
US President Donald Trump praised the arrests, stating in Illinois that the suspects were looking to do big damage and had been under review for a long time.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned in July that any UK base used in strikes against Iran would be a legitimate target.
RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire is being used by the US Air Force to launch strikes against Iranian missile sites targeting ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

clusters.headline_hint: Powerful nor'easter storm batters US East Coast causing flooding and power outages

claims.text: Tidal surges swamped low-lying coastal areas in New Jersey, while wind gusts toppled trees on New York's Long Island.
More than 100,000 customers across the Northeast and mid-Atlantic lost power during the nor'easter storm on Sunday.
More than 250 flights were cancelled at Boston Logan International Airport by late Sunday morning as wind gusts reached 64 km/h.
A 56-year-old New York City housing authority employee was killed on Saturday in Brooklyn when a tree fell on him in a parking lot.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a state of emergency covering eight counties including the Bronx, Kings, Nassau, New York, Queens, Richmond, Suffolk, and Westchester.
FlightAware reported more than 5,000 flight delays and nearly 550 cancellations across the US due to the storm.
High tides combined with a full moon and strong winds pushed ocean water inland, causing coastal flooding from Long Island to New Jersey.
Moderate flooding occurred on Saturday night at the Battery on the southern tip of Manhattan.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani stated that New York City had spent one-third of the year facing flood threats.
States of emergency were declared in New York and New Jersey as the nor'easter brought strong winds and coastal flooding.
The Global Citizen Festival concert in Central Park and an Ed Sheeran concert at Gillette Stadium near Boston were cancelled due to severe weather.
About five inches (13 cm) of rain was forecast for parts of Massachusetts, equivalent to more than a month's worth of rainfall.

clusters.headline_hint: Swiss voters overwhelmingly reject referendum proposal for stricter military neutrality

claims.text: Swiss neutrality was internationally recognised at the Congress of Vienna in 1815 following the defeat of Napoleon.
Switzerland codified its military neutrality in 1907, but joined EU sanctions against Russia in 2022.
More than 70% of Swiss voters rejected a referendum proposal that would have barred Switzerland from imposing sanctions without UN approval.
The initiative for stricter neutrality was promoted by the right-wing Swiss People's Party (SVP) and opposed by the federal government and major parties.
Swiss Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis stated during a televised debate that neutrality has always been applied with a degree of flexibility and does not mean indifference.
Neutrality was legally defined for Switzerland by the Hague Convention of 1907, which forbade supplying weapons to countries at war.
All cantons and approximately 70% of voters rejected enshrining a strictly defined version of neutrality into the Swiss constitution.
The rejected proposal would have prohibited Switzerland from joining military alliances or imposing sanctions on warring states unless mandated by the UN.
SVP backer Christoph Blocher reportedly spent 2 million Swiss francs (€2.1 million) supporting the neutrality referendum campaign.
Green Party lawmaker Sibel Arslan welcomed the vote results, stating that voters understood the SVP wanted Switzerland to isolate itself internationally.

clusters.headline_hint: Violent student protests erupt at Punjab's Lovely Professional University following rape allegations

claims.text: Punjab Police deployed over 2,000 personnel at Lovely Professional University after student protests over an alleged rape turned violent.
ADGP M F Farooqui stated that police personnel would remain deployed on the LPU campus through the night to maintain security.
Protesting students pelted stones at police personnel and attacked police vehicles outside LPU on Sunday evening.
Protesting LPU students blocked National Highway 44 outside the university starting around 8 am on Sunday.
Police used a lathi charge to attempt to clear protesting students blocking National Highway 44.
Two police vehicles were set on fire during the LPU campus protests.
Jalandhar Police Commissioner Satinder Singh stated that reports of disturbances inside LPU hostels were rumours and checks found no such incidents.
Lovely Professional University postponed its mid-term examinations and suspended regular classes for 10 days starting September 28.
Student protests at Lovely Professional University in northern India erupted following social media claims that a female student was raped at a girls' hostel by a worker.
Lovely Professional University denied the allegations of rape on campus, describing them as rumours.
LPU Registrar Dr. Monika Gulati released a video featuring three female students residing in Room 504 of Girls' Hostel 3 who denied that any assault took place in their room.
A subsequent video emerged showing the three female students from Room 504 stating that LPU administration instructed them on what to say and posted their video without consent.
Jalandhar Rural SSP Harvinder Singh Virk stated that four to five police vehicles were damaged in the violence.
DIG Naveen Singla stated police registered a case based on statements that a female student was sexually assaulted around three days prior and returned home.
During Sunday evening protests at LPU, academic buildings were torched and explosions were heard from inside the campus.
DIG Naveen Singla stated that protesting students raised concerns regarding a student from Telangana who died by suicide on the LPU campus a fortnight prior.
Punjab Police registered an FIR containing rape charges against unknown persons and constituted a special investigation team to probe allegations.
Protesting LPU students demanded that university founder-chancellor and Rajya Sabha MP Ashok Mittal personally come to the protest site to assure action.
Protests erupted a day earlier at Chitkara University in Patiala over social media rumours alleging two female students died by suicide.

clusters.headline_hint: Bank unions call off three-day nationwide strike after reaching understanding with IBA

claims.text: Bank unions called off a proposed three-day nationwide strike after the Indian Banks Association agreed to form a high-level committee to deliberate on declaring remaining Saturdays as holidays.
State-run bank branches operated on Sunday following government orders to ensure bank customers were not inconvenienced ahead of the planned strike.
The United Forum of Bank Unions deferred its planned nationwide strike from September 28–30 following a meeting with the Indian Banks' Association at 9:30 pm on Sunday, September 27.
The Reserve Bank of India approved the operation of bank branches, offices, ATM-linked branches, and currency chests on Sunday, September 27.
Indian bank branches are currently closed on the second and fourth Saturdays of every month while other Saturdays remain working days.
The IBA and UFBU agreed to begin discussions on modifying the Performance Linked Incentive scheme for officers in Scale IV and above.
AIBEA General Secretary C. H. Venkatachalam stated that all banks will function normally and there will be no strike.
An online meeting lasting about one hour was held between seven bank union representatives and six banking executives on Sunday night.
Devidas Tuljapurkar, chairperson of All India Bank of Maharashtra Employees' Federation, expressed satisfaction over the decision to form a committee regarding a five-day work week.
The proposed three-day bank strike was scheduled to begin on Monday and coincide with the half-yearly closing period for banks.

clusters.headline_hint: Political row erupts in Delhi after Minister Parvesh Verma slaps man during road inspection

claims.text: A political row erupted after a video surfaced showing Delhi PWD Minister Parvesh Verma allegedly slapping a man during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar.
AAP MLA Jarnail Singh attended the road inspection in Tilak Nagar and questioned the quality of the road after pulling out sections of its surface by hand.
Saheb Singh, who handles social media for AAP MLA Jarnail Singh, alleged that Parvesh Verma snatched his phone, hit him, and security personnel grabbed him by the neck.
Delhi PWD Minister Parvesh Verma claimed AAP workers hurled abuses at his family during the inspection and alleged MLA Jarnail Singh sought a commission from PWD engineers.
Delhi AAP chief Saurabh Bharadwaj was detained by police during a protest in Tilak Nagar over the incident.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused the BJP government of using force against people who question authority following the slap incident in Tilak Nagar.
Former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal demanded the arrest of Minister Parvesh Verma and announced plans to inspect the Tilak Nagar road.
Delhi BJP media head Praveen Shankar Kapoor claimed Saheb Singh is a habitual offender previously arrested for allegedly assaulting an MCD employee.
Parvesh Verma was seen slapping a man in Delhi.
Scroll.in reported Parvesh Sahib Singh Verma as holding the position of Delhi Deputy Chief Minister.
Saheb Singh stated that he and AAP MLA Jarnail Singh went to the Tilak Nagar site after being called by the Public Works Department to inspect the road.
Saheb Singh submitted a formal complaint against Delhi PWD Minister Parvesh Verma at Vikaspuri Police Station.
Saheb Singh stated, 'If any evidence emerges that I used abusive language, I am ready to turn myself in for arrest; I have stated this clearly.'
AAP MLA Jarnail Singh demanded a CBI inquiry into the Tilak Nagar road project and called for Parvesh Verma's immediate suspension.
